summary: Focused bevy_app 0.20.0 guidance for reusable synchronous plugins and caller-driven simulation schedules, with default features disabled and std enabled. The recipes use bevy_ecs =0.20.0 with the same feature selection. Browser rendering, web bindings, networking, asynchronous plugin readiness, fixed wall-clock pacing, and deterministic replay are outside this coverage. Analysis is imported from frozen published-crate evidence; no separate agent review is recorded.

findings.title: Configure reusable behavior through Plugin::build
findings.guidance: Plugin::build configures the App when the plugin is registered. Both fn(&mut App) and a struct implementing Plugin work; plugins are unique by default. Put resource and system registration in build, and expose game configuration through the plugin type. The recipe uses synchronous setup; callers embedding App must respect readiness, finish, and cleanup for plugins that need them.

findings.title: Creating a schedule does not schedule its execution
findings.guidance: init_schedule creates a missing schedule and edit_schedule can configure it. The Main schedule only runs labels listed in MainScheduleOrder. For caller-driven ticks, run the custom schedule explicitly; for a phase inside App::update, insert its label into MainScheduleOrder. App::update is one update call, not a wall-clock fixed-timestep guarantee.

findings.title: Use the 0.20.0 executor API
findings.guidance: The published MainSchedulePlugin configures simple facilitator schedules with schedule.set_executor(SingleThreadedExecutor::new()). The recipes apply the same release-specific API to custom schedules. Single-threaded execution alone does not establish deterministic query order or deterministic cross-platform simulation.

findings.title: Keep the simulation feature set explicit
findings.guidance: The bevy_app default feature set includes reflection, bevy_ecs defaults, and the error panic hook. These recipes disable defaults on both component crates and enable std. The separately declared web feature adds platform web support and browser dependencies; the minimal simulation recipes do not provide a browser event loop or browser API integration. Cargo feature unification can enable additional features in a larger consumer graph.

recipes.title: Drive a plugin-owned simulation schedule explicitly
recipes.description: A synchronous plugin installs a custom schedule with the 0.20.0 SingleThreadedExecutor API. An external caller advances exactly three simulation ticks. It supplies no wall-clock pacing, networking, renderer, or browser event loop.

recipes.title: Insert a custom phase into App::update
recipes.description: A function plugin places a custom schedule immediately after Update so every caller-driven App::update executes it once. The counter assertion distinguishes initialization from actual execution; it is not a fixed-rate clock.
